title: Parallel track: deployment, design, and environment hardening

comments.author: home
comments.text:
PURPOSE: work that can proceed INDEPENDENTLY of the renderer critical path (PPY-92f846), so a swarm of agents can make progress while the orchestrating session is rate-limited.

RULES FOR ANYONE PICKING UP FROM THIS EPIC:
- Read PPY-92f846's HANDOFF comment first for repo/branch/push state and the decided nomenclature (Renderer x Layout). Do not relitigate settled decisions.
- These tasks are deliberately scoped to NOT collide with the renderer work. Do not refactor lib/renderer.ts or renderers/pretext/ from here; if you must, comment on PPY-92f846 instead of editing.
- Report findings as Kanbus comments as you go, not only at the end. The orchestrator may be throttled; Kanbus is the shared state.
- Do not push and do not open PRs without Ryan's explicit say-so. Everything is local on feature/renderer-architecture (Papyrus) and feature/document-ir (Markus), neither pushed.
- Ryan endorsed working directly in AnthusAI/Papyrus. Not a fork.
- Do not close your own issue; comment your findings and leave it for review.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
=== READY QUEUE - PICK UP FROM HERE IF THE ORCHESTRATOR IS THROTTLED ===

These are specced, unblocked, and deliberately chosen NOT to collide with the renderer critical path. Each issue's own comment is the authoritative spec. Take one, comment that you have taken it, work, comment findings as you go.

CURRENTLY RUNNING (do not touch these files):
- PPY-a10206 + PPY-88f77b - IR ingestion, Pretext projection, Markus renderer, real published pages. Touches lib/, renderers/. AVOID.
- PPY-5e8072 - Pilobil.us visual design. Touches /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us + Markus CSS. AVOID.

AVAILABLE NOW, ordered by value:

1. PPY-6b4094 - Deploy Papyrus to AWS, report rough edges. HIGHEST VALUE of the available set. We currently cannot tell real regressions from environment noise: 'npm run build' fails identically on origin/develop and on our branch because no AppSync backend is reachable. A real deployment is the only way to get a trustworthy baseline. Creates real AWS resources - use a sandbox, record teardown, never touch production. Model: Sonnet or better (judgment-heavy, unpredictable failure modes).

2. PPY-fd8468 - Repair the BDD environment. Two known pre-existing causes: features/operator-cli.feature has ZERO cucumber-js step definitions (it targets 'poetry run behave'), and console scenarios lack seeded GraphQL data. Coordinate with PPY-6b4094 - a real backend may fix the second outright. Model: Sonnet.

3. PPY-61dc8f - Persisted reader setting 'newspaper' silently resets after the newsprint rename. Small, tightly specified, disjoint files (amplify/functions/reader-settings/). GOOD HAIKU CANDIDATE - the fix is spelled out (accept the old value as a deprecated alias normalizing to newsprint, plus a test). Verify the premise first: confirm persisted data actually exists before migrating an empty table.

4. PPY-f25738 - Decide the lib/ -> renderers/ layering inversion. Genuinely a judgment call, not mechanical. Best deferred until PPY-eca592 lands, since option (b) needs a resolvable active renderer. Model: Sonnet or better. LOW priority.

STILL BLOCKED (do not start):
- PPY-eca592 (renderer config discriminated union) - would collide head-on with the running a10206/88f77b work. Wait.
- PPY-b794e1 (migrate existing content) - needs a10206's projection to exist first.
- PPY-10e4cd (Pilobil PoC) - needs 88f77b + eca592.

MODEL GUIDANCE FROM RYAN: use Haiku where the work is simple BECAUSE the task is already spelled out exactly. Use Sonnet or better where failure modes are unpredictable (deployment, environment repair) or where real judgment is required (design, architecture decisions). Do not use a small model just because an issue is short - use it when the issue is UNAMBIGUOUS.

STANDING RULES: do not push, do not open PRs, do not close your own issue, commit in small reviewable increments rather than leaving a large uncommitted tree, and re-run verification rather than trusting a summary.
